(Image for representative purpose only) 8th Pay Commission news: The All India Railwaymen's Federation (AIRF) has requested an additional two days with 8th Pay Commission chairperson Ranjana Prakash Desai to discuss matters concerning railway employees across several categories, including medical personnel, traffic department staff, ministerial employees and supervisors in technical departments. Separately, the All India Defence Employees’ Federation (AIDEF) is scheduled to meet the 8th Pay Commission on November 18. Discussions are expected to cover salaries, pensions, allowances, insurance and other matters affecting employees. In a letter dated November 12, 2026, AIRF secretary general Shiva Gopal Mishra sought a further two-day appointment with the commission to take up various employee-related issues. The railway employees' federation has already held discussions with the 8th Pay Commission, with its most recent meeting taking place on October 31. It had also submitted its memorandum to the commission on October 10 this year. According to an ET report, in its latest communication, AIRF listed the employee categories it wants to discuss at the proposed meeting: Medical department: All non-gazetted categories of railway medical employees.
 Supervisory staff in technical departments: Supervisors across all technical departments of Indian Railways , including drawing and design personnel, CMT staff, Depot Material Superintendents (DMS) and the Information Technology (IT) cadre.
 Traffic department: All non-gazetted employees in the department, including Controllers and other categories, except train managers.
 Ministerial staff: Ministerial cadres, excluding accounts personnel, along with stenographers, staff and welfare inspectors, and works study inspectors.
 Accounts and miscellaneous categories: Accounts employees and other miscellaneous categories of railway staff.
 Other railway establishments and specialised categories: Employees of Metro Railway, Kolkata, the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), Rajbhasha categories and other such groups.
 AIRF has argued that the categories it has identified account for a significant portion of the railway workforce and have specific job responsibilities and service-related concerns. It said their views must also be adequately represented before the commission so that their legitimate demands receive proper consideration under the 8th Pay Commission (CPC). “Accordingly, we request that at least two additional days may kindly be earmarked for detailed discussions on the above-mentioned categories, at a date and time convenient to the Hon'ble Chairperson and the Commission,” the AIRF wrote.  AIDEF demands from 8th Pay Commission
 The All India Defence Employees’ Federation (AIDEF), which represents around 50,000 civilian defence employees, is scheduled to meet the 8th CPC on November 18. The federation intends to press for an end to the disparity between railway employees and civilian defence personnel in pay scales and promotion opportunities. It argues that civilian defence employees require a high level of skill and work under hazardous conditions. C Srikumar, general secretary of AIDEF, shared with ET a list of demands he intends to raise during the meeting with the pay commission. These include: Minimum pay: Set the minimum salary at Rs 69,000, using a fitment factor of 3.83 and a five-unit family as the basis for calculation.
 Promotions: Ensure a minimum of five promotions or Assured Career Progression (ACP) benefits over 30 years of service.
 Risk and hardship allowance: Provide an allowance of Rs 10,000 per month.
 Group insurance: Increase the insurance cover to Rs 1 crore for Group C employees, Rs 1.5 crore for Group B employees and Rs 3 crore for Group A employees.
 Compensation for death on duty: Provide ex-gratia compensation of Rs 2 crore to employees killed in accidents while on duty.
 Compassionate appointments: Make compassionate appointments available in 100% of eligible cases.
 Medical facilities: Provide cashless medical treatment, including access to the latest medical and surgical procedures.
 Pension scheme: Withdraw the National Pension System (NPS) and Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), and restore the Old Pension Scheme (OPS).
 Pension revision: Revise pensions for those who retired before January 1, 2026, restore the commuted portion of pension after 12 years and increase pensions every five years.
